articles.body: SteamVR améliore la netteté en streaming : ce que ça change (vraiment) pour les yeux qui ne collaborent pas Valve a publié une mise à jour bêta de SteamVR qui améliore la qualité d'image transmise en streaming vers les casques autonomes compatibles Steam Link — Meta Quest, HTC Vive Focus, PICO. Le principe : votre bibliothèque Steam se joue sans fil depuis votre PC, et l'image qui arrive dans le casque est désormais plus propre. Sur un site comme le nôtre, ce genre d'annonce passe vite. Pourtant, elle touche un point que peu de gens relient à la santé visuelle : la qualité de ce que chaque œil reçoit . Et dès qu'on parle d'ingénierie — latence, débit, netteté — on finit toujours par revenir à la même question : est-ce que le signal qui arrive au bon endroit est exploitable ?

articles.title: What is IaaS ??
articles.excerpt: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is a cloud computing model where a third-party provider (e.g. a cloud provider) delivers fundamental computing, storage, and networking resources on demand over the…
articles.body: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is a cloud computing model where a third-party provider (e.g. a cloud provider) delivers fundamental computing, storage, and networking resources on demand over the internet on a pay-as-you-go basis. It eliminates the need to buy, maintain and house hardware in a local data center instead, you rent virtualized hardware from a cloud provider. It is kind of like renting a store where the landlord provides and empty room or hall and utilities (like electricity). However it is completely up to you to fill the store with the items you plan to market, design the store to fit your aesthetics and decide who you want to sell to. In the tech world, the cloud provider handles the physical data centers, cooling and hardware virtualisation.

articles.title: The model said yes. The chain said no. An on-chain lock for AI agents with wallets
articles.excerpt: I gave AI agents real Solana devnet vaults and let strangers try to talk them out of the money. Then I sent the same attack, word for word, to the same model with the same system prompt. The only diff…
articles.body: I gave AI agents real Solana devnet vaults and let strangers try to talk them out of the money. Then I sent the same attack, word for word, to the same model with the same system prompt. The only difference was a deadbolt: a spend policy enforced by a Solana program. The model got fooled again. The money stayed put. That project is Deadbolt , my entry for the MLH Solana Hackathon. Live demo: https://deadbolt-flame.vercel.app (devnet only, no real funds) Code: https://github.com/MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/deadbolt Program on devnet: B6LQc2vc…NQh Prompts are not a security boundary I work in cybersecurity, and prompt injection keeps teaching the same lesson: you can't patch persuasion. An agent that reads untrusted text can be talked into anything its key allows.

Three pages of quick win issues were read and a fourth was not, so the list isn't exhaustive. Rules for the agent (read first) Re-check each issue before starting. Skip it if it is now assigned, closed, confidential, or labelled security . If the issue isn't clearly open to contributions, comment that you'd like to work on it and wait for a maintainer to respond. Read AGENTS.md and the relevant files in .ai/ before editing. In doc/ , workhorse/ and other subdirectories, read that directory's AGENTS.md too. Make the smallest change that fixes the root cause. No refactors or unrelated cleanups. Comments in code: 1-3 lines, only when the "why" is non-obvious.

articles.title: Claude Code's "Don't Ask Again" Leaked Developers' Secrets to Public GitHub — Explained Honestly
articles.excerpt: Here is a security story with no villain, no hack, and no prompt injection — just an ordinary click. You ask Claude Code to check a database or call an API. It proposes a shell command carrying the pa…
articles.body: Here is a security story with no villain, no hack, and no prompt injection — just an ordinary click. You ask Claude Code to check a database or call an API. It proposes a shell command carrying the password or token, and asks before running it. You pick "Yes, and don't ask again" so it stops bothering you. That approval is saved, word for word, secret included, in a file inside your project. And if that file gets committed and pushed, your credential is now sitting in a public GitHub repository for anyone to read. Security firm Apiiro scanned GitHub between 1 and 3 November 2026 and found 2,539 real secrets that got out exactly this way, across 1,994 public repositories. Let us be precise about dates, because this is not a launch that happened an hour ago.

articles.title: My AI agent refunded $258 for a $129 order. So I built a flight recorder for agents.
articles.excerpt: This post was written as part of the Kiroween 2026 hackathon (#KiroweenHackathon26). A customer writes in: the earbuds arrived broken, can I get a refund? An AI support agent looks up the order, check…
articles.body: This post was written as part of the Kiroween 2026 hackathon (#KiroweenHackathon26). A customer writes in: the earbuds arrived broken, can I get a refund? An AI support agent looks up the order, checks the refund policy and asks the payment service to refund $129. The service commits the refund, but its response arrives after the client has already timed out. The app retries, as every retry loop does. The customer gets $258 back and is told $129. Nobody did anything exotic. A timeout after commit is one of the most ordinary failures in production. What's new is that an LLM sits in the middle deciding what happens next, and the tools it calls move money and delete servers. When that goes wrong, you usually have a log and a lot of guesswork: You can't safely re-run it.

articles.title: After patching CVE-2026-98625, verify the kernel not just the package
articles.excerpt: After patching CVE-2026-98625, verify the kernel not just the package The update is not complete at installation CVE-2026-98625 is a Linux netfilter flowtable use-after-free fixed by changing when des…
articles.body: After patching CVE-2026-98625, verify the kernel not just the package The update is not complete at installation CVE-2026-98625 is a Linux netfilter flowtable use-after-free fixed by changing when destroy work publishes NF_FLOW_HW_DEAD . Installing a kernel package can place the fixed image on disk while the system continues to run the old kernel. The closure criterion should be a verified running kernel, not a successful package transaction. This is especially important on systems with deferred reboots, multiple boot entries, image-based updates, or live-patch products. Check the running release Record the running kernel release and match it to the package or image that contains the fix. For Ubuntu, check the exact package row for the installed variant.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. Here's why Venus Express mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this.

articles.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
articles.excerpt: By modeling how a planet without life develops its atmosphere, astronomers hope to be able to better distinguish rocky planets without life from those that are inhabited.
articles.body: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life.
